prompt: Some people say that the fashion industry is bad for the environment, as it encourages consumers to buy new clothes all the time. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is argued that the fashion industry damages the environment by encouraging consumers to purchase new clothes frequently. I largely agree with this view because the industry’s marketing and production models promote unnecessary consumption. However, consumers should also bear some responsibility for the environmental consequences of their shopping choices.

Admittedly, the fashion industry has a negative impact on the environment through aggressive marketing strategies. By constantly introducing new collections and presenting existing clothes as outdated, companies encourage consumers to replace their clothes frequently. This creates excessive demand and leads manufacturers to produce garments on a massive scale. The production of cheap fast-fashion items consumes substantial amounts of water and energy and may also release harmful chemicals into rivers. Moreover, low-quality garments are often discarded after being worn only a few times, increasing the amount of textile waste sent to landfills.

Nevertheless, the fashion industry should not be regarded as the only cause of this problem, as consumer behaviour also sustains the cycle of excessive production and waste. If shoppers choose durable clothing and resist every new fashion trend, manufacturers will have less incentive to produce such large quantities of clothes. Similarly, growing demand for sustainably produced garments may encourage companies to use recycled materials and adopt cleaner manufacturing methods. Consumers can therefore either strengthen or reduce the environmental impact of the industry through their purchasing decisions.

In conclusion, I largely agree that the fashion industry is environmentally harmful because it actively promotes frequent consumption. Nevertheless, consumers also contribute to the problem, so both companies and shoppers need to change their behaviour.
